t:
I'm here to warn you. And maybe give you a few pointers.

For me, all the events that are happening in there right now are the past. I know exactly what happened - and I can tell you what will happen. If you agree to go on this adventure. Or maybe it won't be you, but someone else? The future has many facets.

Of course, I won't stop you if you want to do everything on your own - after all, as one of our mutual acquaintances likes to say, the real Truth is attained only through one's own efforts and only such truth can be considered a World Mystery.

However, those efforts don't have to be strenuous - maybe you should come back here later when you're older and stronger...

Are you interested?

Oh, this is one of my favorite stories. First of all, I like the main character - eternally young, brave, curious, beautiful... Okay, let's stop there.

But this story intrigues me. It's very simple. There is evil and there are heroes who go out to fight this evil. No ambiguity, no grey areas.

Will you become its hero? You did. I saw it. Will you take the plunge now, or will you find out how it all ends from me?
r512955.n: Oh, this is one of my favorite stories. First of all, I like the main…

t: It's an inappropriate thing to say to a guest, especially one from the future. The fate of Sarnaut is decided here, and even the gods are involved, so I couldn't miss it. Well, do you want to know what kind of bait our God of Darkness hid in the center of the Dead City? The one that attracted the Wormfaces, demons, and Draconids there? It even drew the Servant of Tensess out of Purgatory.

So, where were we? Perhaps, while traveling through these islands of Umoir, you have forgotten how it all began...

During the final battle with Tep, Klavdia Kalugina captured his Spark and then disappeared. The leaders of the League and the Empire, concerned about this, sent you after Klavdia.

The trail led you right here, to the League allod Umoir which was controlled by the Great Sorceress Catherina. Umoir is afflicted by a strange disease - the Blight which infects both animals and plants, turning them into monsters. In addition, Catherina is in conflict with adherents of old beliefs, trying to spread faith in the Light.

You managed to find out the following:

First, Klavdia used the power of Tep's Spark to establish her cult and faith in her as a protector. She's trying to gain as much power as possible. Did you really think she was bad? Tsk tsk!

Second, the Old Gods of Umoir really exist, and their power also depends on faith in them.

Third, some incomprehensible threat is approaching, and even the gods fear it.

In the end, you managed to reconcile the adherents of the old and new faith. However, the moment it happened, you were attacked by demons. In addition, the doors of Catherina's tower closed, and her guards began to attack anyone who tried to enter. After you finally managed to get into the tower, an unpleasant surprise awaited you there.

I have to retell the story once again...

"Catherina serves Sarn who created the Blight. There's no doubt about it. I do not care whether is was a conscious decision or not, but that doesn't matter. What matters is that the Eclipse is about to sail off to the heart of the world where Sarn is imprisoned. And I don't think it's a social visit! I'm sure she has keys to the Seals. Maybe not all of them, but even one broken Seal would be enough. My father is far away from this world, so no one would be able to stop the Prisoner. If he breaks free, Sarnaut is doomed!"

Of course, you had to follow her! Follow Catherina!
r512957.n: Yes, I want to know what will happen if I go after the Eclipse.

t:

But you're probably wondering what will happen if you step onto the pier and go after the Eclipse?

If you want to know, you can just ask...

You are not dealing with mad gods or feisty sorceresses this time! You are on the forgotten Ferris, where the Tungars live in the ice. These savages worship their barbarian deities. Strength is the only thing they respect.

You managed to piss them off. You captured their camp, insulted their deities, and beat up their leader. They can't wait to pay you back. Alas, the Historians are no match for you, and as soon as you leave the camp, it will be defenseless. And if the Tungars break in here, they will slaughter everyone.

The solution: strike first. Go to their camp and deal with them.

t:
So what is the Bestiary?

The Empire's secret training ground where they performed experiments on various local animals. The key part of these experiments was an object that was found in that very lake, enclosed in a piece of a meteorite. The Imperials used it on test subjects with varying degrees of success. As you can see, that worm, the "Specimen", managed to escape in the end. It settled somewhere around here.

Meanwhile, the local animals started to suffer from some kind of disease. They began to turn into "modificants". Do you remember the Blight? Wait, it's not that simple!

I'll remind you about something else - on the Eclipse, when you fought Captain Krivov, his construct turned into some kind of creature that emanated the air of "order", right? Does anything here seem familiar to you?

Okay, let’s get back to business. Finding an entrance to the Bestiary was not easy. You were lucky. This is how Herbert put it:

"One of our jaegers, Sergey Dozorin, sent me a message yesterday. He has found another entrance to the Bestiary. He has somehow activated a Portal in a cave in the Deadly Frostland. The Tungars use that cave it for their pagan rituals. And we have both seen what Tungar gods are capable of...

I don't think you will be able to get past them undetected like Dozorin did, but you can always fight your way through. Maas-Tyna the Light-Footed in our first camp can show you the way.

The Bestiary might have answers to many of our questions, so we can't miss this opportunity to find them."

Herbert decided to deal with Negus Jeeg who apparently played a key role in the fate of this Laboratory.

But before we could get to this mad Zem, we had to deal with the Mechanoid sentries and Herbert's clone.

Too bad we don't have enough time.

t:
I can't miss your first foray into the world of the Architects... Well, I don't know if it can be called a world. More like ordered space.

Do you believe the Sculptor? You'll have to trust his word.

So, do you want to know what will happen if you follow him to the Otherverse?

Hmm, what do we have here? A war?

So, you took the heroic path, defeated the enemy, and locked him up in his last refuge. The final onslaught is still ahead.

The Architects. Or rather, the Architect. I don't think the number matters here. They came from another world to bring Absolute Order. Renounce chaos, relinquish movement, relinquish free will, embrace stasis and ultimate... eternal... order.

The Architect has a collective mind. It's complex and lies beyond human comprehension. The basis of each combat unit is the Core. It contains part of the united consciousness. Everything else is just a shell that performs the necessary function. Destruction of living beings, for example.

The Architect's technologies are unknown. But there's one thing we know for sure. They can somehow absorb and transform any biological substance into graphite-like stone or possibly metal which they use to create their shells.

The Architect can build different shell configurations depending on the desired function. From a small "emitter" to a large siege structure... And most importantly, the Archonts.

But you probably want to know the ending. What happens if you enter the Fractal space?

t:
The war is over, but we still need to deal with the consequences, right? At least only Dane was affected.

And what do we have here? More cultists, only this time they worship Order? A strange goblin prophesying a new order?

Let me tell you what others have said:

"I knew there was someone more powerful behind the fanatics and the Prophet. At first I thought it could be a Great Mage, but when I heard them mention the Sculptor - and nobody told me about him for some reason! - everything became clear. However, I can only speculate about the purpose of their experiments. And my speculations are not comforting at all.

As you can remember, faith is a great power which can literally move mountains. The Architects - or should I say the Architect - is using the power of self-assertion. He believes in himself, and he is unflinching in his faith in the special purpose of his mind. But the Sculptor has lost that power when he detached himself from the whole. Now he is trying to compensate by creating monsters who look like him and have infinite faith in his power.

You see what the problem is? If the Sculptor succeeds in creating a sentient chimera using human and Architect flesh, and that creature will be a believer, we will face a catastrophe comparable in scale to the invasion of Dane! This is what the Prophet and the fanatics want - to create an army of chimeras who know no doubt or hesitation and believe in the divinity of the Sculptor."

We need to prevent that before it turns into a global problem... You want to hear the story?

"Well, well, the boy is ambitious. He's barely an adult, but he's ready to go after an immortal being. They grow up so fast...!

Alright, let's be serious. The thing is, Kyros might actually be able to get it done. How do I know that? Does it matter? Well, let’s call it intuition. I can feel a mysterious power in him.

To follow Kyros into the portal, you will have to enter the Well of Souls. Yes, that pillar of light which spawns newborn Aoidoi. My magic will direct you to the Secret Paths, the deepest layer of the Planar Rim. I don't know what's waiting for you down there. If you are lucky, you will find an entrance to the Purgatory. You will be the first mortal in history to enter it alive. And you probably won't enjoy it...

But you're used to it, aren't you?"

There was one problem - the path to the Well was blocked by demons who had no intention of letting you through.

"The time has come. Before the Demon has a chance to raise a new army, we need to enter the tomb and challenge him! Your path lies through the thicket full of the undead. But that's not the worst part. There are only two ways to the tomb, and both of them are extremely dangerous.

One lies through the dead water. A huge ancient toad called Jam lives there.

The other road winds through the burial grounds where an ancient monster dwells. It once used to be a powerful necromancer. Tep was his name, I think... Oh, I see you know that name, don't you?

Choose your path wisely! And take this trinket. Use it to summon me at any time! I'll be with you all the time, unseen. I'll try and warn you if something is wrong. Best of luck to you!"

t:
No one knows for sure. The necromancer Tep, who doomed his people, had conducted a thorough research into the nature of Sparks.

While studying the nature of death, Tep realized that every creature had a certain essence, a spark of life which was enclosed in the body and left it with death. Many called this Spark a "soul" or "divine essence", but Tep tried to approach this issue more practically. He learned to catch other people's Sparks to use their power and gain immortality.

Sages say a lot about Sparks - that they are a part of every soul, that it's a gift that grants free will. It is also believed that Sparks cannot be destroyed. That even when extinguished, they leave a tiny particle that can be reignited and filled with power. That their power comes from the very essence of the world, forming a single whole with its soul.

"Sparks are incomprehensible because they cannot be comprehended, indestructible because they cannot be destroyed," Tensess himself once said.

Perhaps you are interested in something else... Are there creatures without Sparks? Yes, those are the undead, all kinds of zombies and ghouls, just dead bodies filled with the power of a necromancer who raises them. They only have the memory of their body. It's a different person in every other regard. But there are cases when the Spark returns to its dead body - that's how it happened with the Zem people.

Ghosts, on the other hand, are a completely different phenomenon... Some ghosts are just an echo, a replica of the events of the past revived thanks to magic. Such ghosts also don't have Sparks, although they are often filled with the energy of their reflection. But there are rebellious souls, the ether body and the Spark linked together - they cannot leave our world and are forced to exist in this form.

Soon after the Cataclysm, the Great Mages noticed a strange phenomenon, clearly of a magical nature. The time of its emergence indicated that it was somehow connected to the Astral.

The Astral was magically affecting the inhabitants of Sarnaut. The twelve tides of that force were detected. Each had different properties and impacted the people in its own way. Without any doubt, the phenomenon was a result of the Cataclysm.

For a long time, there was no unity among the Great Mages on the issue of the nature of this phenomenon. Many of them conducted experiments in an effort to confirm their theory. All these theoretical studies had practical results. It soon became clear that a resident of Sarnaut could undergo initiation by becoming the "carrier" of one specific tide. This magical symbiosis grants the initiate special abilities and powers. It was quite easy to distinguish one adept from another: those affected by the wave acquired a distinctive magical glowing halo.

For a long time, the secret of the "astral tides" remained unsolved, and only in the tenth century of the New Era, the truth was revealed.

During the Cataclysm, many Great Mages died, and the mechanism for containing the Astral was not developed for some time. It took the lives of twelve members of the Conclave to curb the Astral. But when humans or elves become Great Mages, they gain immortality! It was immortality that allowed the Spark of Tensess to survive in the Astral and gave it the strength to take control of Tep's Pyramid. And knowing this, how can one consider it a coincidence that after the Cataclysm exactly twelve astral tides appeared - which is the number of dead Great Mages who had developed the Astral Containment Ritual!

Skrakan and Zayan remembered their names. The names of those who, like Tensess himself, served the world even after their death. Their sacrifice was not in vain. Their power is constantly present in the world, giving the Great Mages the ability to hold allods and granting the people of Sarnaut a part of their strength. In the year 921 of the New Age, the names of the Twelve Martyrs were declared, and each force tide was given a name. Anyone could pass the ritual of initiation and become an adept of one of the forces. That's how the mystical Institute of the Twelve Martyrs was established.

The people of Sarnaut believe in their Patrons - the Twelve Great Martyrs who gave their lives in the name of saving the world and bestowed their blessing upon every living creature. Each inhabitant of the allods goes through the Initiation Ritual when they reach a certain age, becoming an adept of one of the magical forces.

You, too, have undergone this ritual!
r518151.n: Tell me about the twelve Patrons

t:
The Church of the League, also known as the Church of Light, was founded first. Its tenets are based on the fact that the Gift of Tensess and the magic of Light became available to the inhabitants of Sarnaut thanks to the sacrifice of Tensess who died fighting the demons. Tensess's Spark went to Tep's Pyramid and defeated this necromancer, expelling him from the Pyramid.

Using the power of the Pyramid, Tensess granted resurrection to all the inhabitants of Sarnaut.

The Empire did not accept this Gift at first. Even in the time of Nezeb, attempts were made to use the new magic, but it soon became clear that without faith in the sacrifice of Tensess, the Light magic was inaccessible. Nezeb did not instill the new religion in the Empire, not wanting to deify his eternal enemy.

Everything changed after the Great Astral Campaign. In this battle, the soldiers of the Empire fought side by side with the Kanians, and the servants of the Church of Light treated their wounds. Wanting to use the magic of Light, the Xadaganian Committee decided to create their own "Church" where they began to revere Tensess along with Nezeb and Skrakan who died during the Great Astral Campaign.

According to the teachings of this "Trinity Church", the sacrifices of Tensess, Nezeb, and Skrakan were considered equal, and they were all declared great martyrs of the great war. This is how the Empire got its own Church and its own priests using the magic of Light.

Of course, we all understand that it is only thanks to Tensess that this Gift exists. The Empire also understands this. For several years now it has been fighting for the Holy Land where his Temple is located.

Our Church is governed by the Council of Priests which consists of the priests of all allods. The same Council chooses its leader. It's now Voisvet Belov, the templar of the first circle and the governor of the Kanian Archipelago.
r518152.n: What's the difference between the Churches of the League and Empire?

t:
The Church of the League, also known as the Church of Light, was founded first. Its tenets are based on the fact that the Gift of Tensess and the magic of Light became available to the inhabitants of Sarnaut thanks to the sacrifice of Tensess who died fighting the demons. Tensess's Spark went to Tep's Pyramid and defeated this necromancer, expelling him from the Pyramid.

Using the power of the Pyramid, Tensess granted resurrection to all the inhabitants of Sarnaut.

However, was Tensess's sacrifice something unique? Or perhaps Nezeb and Skrakan, who sacrificed themselves in the battle against demons, are no different from Tensess? Could the Great Nezeb forget about his followers even in death?

Our Trinity Church teaches sensibly: Tensess's sacrifice is equal to the sacrifice of Nezeb and Skarkan. All of them are great martyrs of the great war.

The Church of the League refused to accept Nezeb as a saint, even though they recognize the sainthood of the five Imperial Great Mages who died when the world split into allods. The thing is, corrupt hierarchs are afraid... afraid of the truth, because everyone understands that the Empire is superior to the League in everything!

In addition, our Church is based on equality: we do not have Superiors; we have commissars and political leaders who are equal in rights, and the same goes for church ministers of other nations of the Empire. Each of these political leaders can head the respective committee after a closed and secret ballot. In the rotten League everything is controlled through nepotism and bribery.

Now Elizaveta Rysina, the head of the City Council, has taken over the helm of the Church Affairs Committee.
r518153.n: What's the difference between the Churches of the League and Empire?

t:
You understand, all these events with the gods left their mark. Many witnessed what was happening in our world, many saw the battle of the mad Kyros and Servant of Tensess! Demons, Architects, the appearance of the Aoidoi - all this needed explanation.

After long negotiations, the Church of Light and the Trinity Church decided to unite. As for dogmas, we have yet to establish them. It's clear that there is something outside of our world that we have no idea about. However, it is clear that the Light is one for everyone - for the League, the Empire, the Pridens, and even the Tekyan. To find the Source of this Light - that's the purpose of the new Church! The Church of the Eternal Light...

It will be led by a collegial body - the Synod of Hierarchs. It will include representatives of each of the races who believe in the Light.
r518154.n: Why did the Churches of the League and the Empire unite?

t:
Light Magic is another commodity granted by Tensess. What makes it different from other magic is the fact that it's available to anyone. The main thing is faith. If you believe in the Light, this magic becomes available to you. And if earlier magic was something few people had access to, now anyone can acquire abilities regardless of their status or knowledge. This changed the balance of power in the world and continues to change it to this day. The Magic of Light is a great power.

Its abilities are diverse - it can both resurrect and heal. But most importantly, it can fight against the enemies of the Light, smiting them.

Very quickly, two directions formed among the inhabitants of Sarnaut: the Priests who were more focused on healing. And the Templars who considered it their duty to protect others.
r518155.n: What is the essence of Light magic?

t:
These brave priestesses are responsible for ensuring that the bodies of the dead are not lost while their Sparks remain in Purgatory.

Each priestess has her own territory which she oversees or asks others to oversee. As soon as she detects a deceased, she transfers them to a special altar where the body will safely await resurrection.

Also, these priestesses heal light and medium wounds using Light magic. In the League they serve in the Order of Mercy, and in the Empire, the Order of Compassion. Of course, although they work selflessly for the benefit of all living, their labors require payment - so they are always ready to sell the holy Mirra needed for donations to the Servant of Tensess.

Wishing to make astral travel safer, these priestesses also enchant cabins on ships. As soon as someone dies in the astral plane, a special spell transfers the deceased to the ship's infirmary where resurrection will take place shortly after. At the request of the Free Traders, similar places are also being set up in various arenas and stadiums.

And if the ship is completely destroyed, the spell can transfer the team to the capital. Of course, maintaining such magic is expensive, but it is paid from the treasury of the state.
r518156.n: What are the duties of the Servants of the Light?

t:
Yes. Unfortunately, not everyone is resurrected...

Firstly, those whose lifespan has come to an end, in old age. Their Sparks go somewhere else...

Secondly, those who reject the Gift of Tensess itself, reject the commandments of the Church, and pose a threat to the whole world cannot be resurrected - like the numerous cultists, demon worshipers, and heretics. But there is an exception - ignorant pagans who do not know about the Gift can be resurrected through the rituals of the priests of the Church. Because if they don't know what they're missing, they can't reject it.

Thirdly, those whose bodies have been irreversibly damaged cannot be resurrected. For example, they dissolved in the astral or were destroyed. The thing is, the Spark needs something to return to. Those who, for example, have their heads cut off cannot be resurrected - such injuries are too severe to be healed.
r518157.n: Is it possible to die permanently?

t:
At the beginning, no one knew about the resurrection. But then an astral ship crashed near the Holy Land. After a heroic death, the sailors found themselves on an unknown allod. "Is this hell, paradise, or non-existence?" they must have asked. Later, they discovered the Tensess Temple. After meeting a smuggler innkeeper, they were able to return to their homeland where they told everyone what happened to them. Cases of resurrection began to multiply.

Those who were able to resurrect said they visited Purgatory and saw a giant fire-headed angel who became known as the Servant of Tensess. It turned out that he releases people from Purgatory only after a certain time which is determined by the sins of the deceased.

But there was also a way to get out ahead of schedule - by donating drops of precious Mirra.

Initially, there was no resurrection in our world. Creatures died, and it was either necromancers who could bring them back in the form of undead, or some complex and dangerous rituals of the Great Mages.

In the year 911 of the Allods Era, an event occurred in Sarnaut that forever changed the usual routine of life - resurrection became possible in case of premature death.

As it turned out in the end, it was a gift from Tensess, the Great Mage of the League, who died in battle during the capture of the capital of Kania. Tensess made this gift not only to the League, but also to the Empire, believing that old enemies should unite in the face of a new external threat.

It happened like this: when the Spark of the Great Tensess, who died during the invasion of demons, ended up in Tep's Pyramid, his strength was enough to repel the ancient evil. The sinister necromancer was banished, and his cursed Pyramid became a temple. Tensess Temple!As it turned out in the end, it was a gift from Tensess, the Great Mage of the League who died in battle during the capture of the capital of Kania. However, after the death of the great Nezeb, our leader and teacher, and of his mentor Skrakan, the power grew - the Light became even more powerful. Nezeb and Skrakan died defending the world against demons, and their sacrifice meant as much as that of Tensess.

His Spark ended up in Tep's Pyramid, and it was powerful enough to repel the ancient evil. The sinister necromancer was banished, and his cursed Pyramid became a temple. Tensess Temple!
r518159.n: Ask about the Gift of Tensess

Well, my advice is simple: do not neglect your gift. Use it. We can take many forms - choose one you like and follow your path.

It all started with demons...

Demons… No one really knows where they came from… It is only known that they have been present in our world for a long time. The famous Great Mage Skrakan encountered the first demon, and it took him great effort to defeat it.

The second time they invaded all allods at once, and this event is now known as the Night of Astral Portals... Millions died...

Then their invasions started happening all the time. No one knew how to deal with them...

No one except us. The truth is simple: sometimes fire can only be fought with fire, and to fight demons... you need to be a bit of a demon yourself.

This path is not for everyone. Only a select few are able to control this power. And you are one of them.

Demonology is a school of magic just like any elemental one. Or witchcraft. Or mysticism. Or necromancy... It doesn't matter - people still look at us like we're lepers, and the Church has imposed penance on us.

But remember this: we are not some crazy cultists. Demons are not our allies or an object of worship. They are no better than guinea pigs. Demons are our window to the world of new magical heights, nothing more.

The material we get from the Astral is pretty good, but to use it most effectively, we need special workpieces. Professions can craft suitable workpieces. Blacksmiths craft armor, leatherworkers make leather, and tailors make cloth. Weaponsmiths craft weapons. There is a fifth type - jewelry workpieces. Any Profession can make those.

But what if you need a workpiece from a Profession you're not trained in? Or you don't want to waste time at some workshop?

There's a solution: ask other players, and they will happily sell you everything you need. There are plenty of lots at the auction, but remember that a seller always sells goods at an upcharge. So a Profession is not just an interesting, but also a profitable occupation.

Over the year, you will gradually unlock better quality workpieces. To learn new recipes, talk to the master of your Profession in the capital.

I looked around at those next to me. Apprentices, future "mechanics", and a number of mechanical knights who are imperfect and clumsy. The transfer of Sparks has proved to be very promising. However, not every Spark will take root in a new body. I need to find a way to contact those Arisen and find out how they get around the issue of "rejection". But Nezeb jealously guards his "scientists". So far, only my first knight remains an ideal model without any flaw.

Sooner or later...

SCARGE WILL BE THE FORCE OF PROGRESS IN KANIA

Therefore, losing a family member is like losing a limb for a family. And our brother died on Coldberg when the undead attacked the mine...

We then turned to that Orc shaman, Kurgan, and he said there's a Ritual of Blood Brotherhood! Which is even stronger than the ritual of fraternity. And with its help, you can unite those who have lost their relatives into one family!

And then the Orc said he'd lied... Orcs don't have a heart! Everyone knows that.

But perhaps he wasn't lying? And this ritual does exist?

t:
Evil storms raged,

White snow fell,

The house stood strong,

Steady and unshakeable.

He who was the oldest

Among the harsh leaders,

Became a father for the first time -

To three brothers.

Thorri was the first,

Lok was next,

Wald came last,

Votin was their father.

Three Gibberlings -

Their sprout was strong!

It was noisy in the house,

Fun every day!

The children were growing up,

Year after year.

Thorri boasted of his strength,

Lok was the most cunning of all.

Wald loved to listen,

Sitting next to his father:

What others say,

Who believes what.

Who brings news

To their home.

At this time,

News was the same:

Hordes of evil Orcs,

Who came uninvited,

Besieged again

the Gibberling lands.

They burn, break, destroy,

Everything that can be touched.

They are getting close

To the Ash Tree.

The Gibberlings seek

Salvation in the sea.

Votin with his troops

Defends the Great Tree.
This rune-covered menhir contains part of an ancient saga...
r519862.n: This rune-covered menhir contains part of an ancient saga...

t:
The years went by

Quickly for the brothers,

And their father's troops

Grew bigger and stronger.

The time came for vengeance

On the Orc people!

The old Votin

Sent the sons to battle.

Thorri chose a hammer

Forged by the Zvergs

And left his father's house

Without saying a word.

Lok said goodbye

To his mother and father,

To his uncles and aunt,

And other relatives.

Wald said a few things

At the threshold of the house.

He promised to return

Once the Orcs were defeated.

The three brothers left,

Watched by sharp eyes.

And words followed them,

Full of spells.

It was a maiden

Of a different kind.

She was called black,

Her fur darker than soot.

Her name was Seida.

Braiding threads

In wonderful patterns,

She saw clearly

Signs and omens

In the Fabric of the Universe.

Regarding the fate of the three brothers

Seida was silent.

t:
Numerous Orcs

Were slain by Thorri's hammer.

Many were scared into fleeing

Straight into Lok's traps.

Then came an avalanche

Of iron shields.

The hird's weapons clanged,

Sharp spears gleamed.

Scarlet flowers

bloomed on Isa's snow.

The Gibberlings' fury

Spared no Orc.

And the enemies fled

In a terrible panic.

It is true that in unity

Was the Gibberlings' strength!

"It's time to go home!"

Thorri told the brothers.

There were spoils:

Silver, gold,

Wonderful armor,

marvelous weapons!

They would have something to show

To Votin and the others!

t:
The journey home was long

The brothers whiled it away

In conversation.

Lok said, thoughtful:

"And where, brothers,

Did these Orcs come from?

Old man told us

They didn't exist!"

"They say the Orcs once lived

In the warm lands of the south

Far away from here.

But they went overseas -

Humans drove them out.

And also dragons,"

Said Wald

who knew the sagas.

"What are Humans?"

Lok asked.

"Humans are Humans,
We have not met them.

But the Orcs know

That somewhere in the south,

Where there is enough land,

There are plenty of them.

There would be even more of them,

If not for the dragons

That burn down

Everything they see.

The dragons feel hatred

For all the living.

The Orc nomads' camps

Died in flames.

After leaving the steppes,

And building boats,

The Orcs moved straight

to Isa as a horde."

The brothers were quiet

For the next part of the journey.

They thought about Orcs,

Humans, and dragons.

t:
The home was now

Only one day away.

Thorri said to Lok

One night in camp,

"I wish we could go back,

Drive the Orcs back to the Humans.

Save our home

From this endless threat.

"That’s right, brother!"

Lok nodded, thinking,

"It’s a pity we are few in number,

And we have no dragons!

I wish we could get

More weapons

From the wise Heidruns,

Praidens, or Zvergs."

They kept going,

Talking all the while

about upcoming battles.

Look - we are home!

In celebration of another victory,

A feast was held.

Brothers were honored,

With raised cups.

Many Gibberlings

Drank beer there,

Ate fish

And a lot of cheese.

And tales were told,

Each better than the last,

Around the mead hall

Deep into the night.

t:
In the morning, early,

When it's dark,

And the fog is still

Over the water,

Three brothers left the house

And went to the square.

They saw a maiden there,

Black as midnight.

"Glorious is your path, brothers!"

That was Seida's voice.

"I ask you to hear

What the Threads promise us."

"Tell me, sister,"

Lok intervened quickly.

"Will we be rid of the Orcs?

Will we drive them out completely?"

Seida answered,

"Sagas will sing about you,

They will carry your feat

Through the centuries to your descendants.

But I see dangers

That threaten the whole of Isa.

Horrible fate awaits us!

The power of insidious Fate!

The Threads of the universe

Tell me this:

Soon the world will plunge

Into the void of oblivion!

The roots of the world will crack,

Rocks will fall into the abyss,

And sea waters

Will boil all at once.

The wolf will swallow the sun,

And the stars will die out.

Darkness will swallow Isa,

devouring everything.

Many souls will die,

Many words will be forgotten,

And the people of Isa

Will perish in the pitch darkness!

That moment is called 'Yok',"

So said Seida.

The brothers fell silent,

Horrified…

t:
"But there are sprouts of hope

Amidst the nightmare,

Seida said again,

"Isa will survive!

A new world will arise

From the wreckage of the old ones,

Great-grandfather, Prophetic Ash Tree

Will be our salvation.

But Fate is treacherous!

Centuries later

Trouble will come again,

Darkness will cover the whole world.

I see it so clearly:

The tree is dying,

The ancient enemy has been awakened,

There is no rest for the dead!

Deadly Frost will come,

And countless enemies

Whose skin is white.

I see it through time.

Blood ties get stronger:

Pilgrim's children

Will take ragged weaving

And tie it into a whole.

And the flower of hope

Will bloom at the Tree,

The news will rush further

To the wonderful land of stars.

This is just the beginning.

I see an ominous city,

It is full of the dead,

Summoned against their will.

Light and darkness in battle

Argue with each other,

But in vain:

Their fate is inevitable.

A new god will rise -

He who took the power

From the unfortunate sisters

Who forgot the law:

What Fate decides

Will happen.

There is no power in the world,

That would change that."

t:
The maiden Seida's

Speeches have faded.

The Gibberling brothers

conferred for a long time.

"You won't scare us!"

Thorri said,

"While my hammer is in my hand,

I will not accept this fate!"

If the pattern is known,

And not yet woven...

We must take the Threads into our hands

And fool Fate!"

So said Lok,

The cunning trickster.

Wald, after much thought,

Supported the idea.

"Since Seida does not know

How to avoid fate,

We will seek advice

from other peoples."

So it was decided,

And there was no reason to delay.

On the same day, the three brothers

Set off on another journey.

t:
The path took them far away,

To the foot of Muspel

Where good Heidruns

settled among the grass.

The Gibberlings were greeted

By Ilko, the chief of the horned ones.

The people welcomed the guests,

Offering mead.

"Tell us, wise one,

How to argue with Destiny?

How to avoid Fate,

What do the Threads say?"

The Heidrun chief said,

"Yes, Fate is harsh.

What it decided to weave

Will surely happen.

We gave this evil force

A different name.

We call it the Weaver

That spins Threads.

But we believe

That another power exists.

It gives a chance

to those it favors.

If Luck loves

Her chosen one,

They will avoid Fate

And deceive the Threads.

But while she falls in love quickly,

She falls out of it just as easily.

The circle will come around again,

And luck will pass.

About the one who created

All the living things.

He rarely appeared,

But whoever saw him knows:

Num is the creator of the living.

He must be wiser than all of us."

"That's right, Ilko,

Since he is the father to all of us,

How to escape fate.

"Num's house is unknown.

But there are signs

That can show the way.

When you see a Rainbow,

He is at the edge

Farthest from you.

Look there.

Where the sky shines,

From horizon to horizon,

Num will be close,

You can find him.

Where the winds were born

And the fires of volcanoes,

There are traces of creation,

And Num's abode.

But those brave ones

Who do not believe in fate

And who want to fight it

Should remember this:

By challenging the might

That is stronger than gods,

Brave madmen

Will bring doom."

"We will not be stopped

By threats of Fate,

A warrior does not fear

Empty words,"

t:
The north received the brothers,

Where the radiance of the sky

Illuminates the earth

But does not warm it.

The path is long and difficult,

The journey took many days.

There is nothing but ice and rocks,

And spoils are scarce.

Every day is shorter

Under the dim sun,

The night grows boundlessly,

Darkness brings cold.

One night a storm

Wakes up the brothers.

A veil of snow

Covers everything around them.

They see through the snowstorm

That someone is approaching -

A silhouette

With a shaky gait.

Once the fire dispelled

The darkness that hid the image,

The brothers were horrified:

It was a frozen corpse!

Features and clan marks were hidden

Under the iron mask.

His armor was covered

With hoarfrost patterns.

t:
Thorri swung his hammer

At the evil spirit!

But suddenly the uninvited guest

Said quietly,

"Who are you and why are you here?"

The brothers were surprised.

"We are Gibberlings

Looking for the house of Num."

Like you, I once searched

For the House of the Creator...

The road was not easy,

I fell, killed by Frost."

"We do not fear Frost!"

Thorri answered.

"It is worth fearing

the Evil God of Cold.

Here he reigns supreme,

Eradicating life.

The deadly frost

Kills outright.

Be afraid to meet

The ice maiden here.

If you look even once

Into the eyes of an Isfrun,

You will turn to ice,

And your life force will fade.

Even the Junes fear

The powers of the harsh ice.

There are many other

Creatures of nightmare here.

Ice worms,

Jotunns and Wargs...

If you go further,

It will be even more dangerous.

Icy expanses

Are not for the living!"

"We will reach our goal,"

Said the brothers.

"The Threads of our Fate

have become stronger!

Thank you for your advice...

What is your name?"

The dead one answered them:

They used to call me Nagle."

t:
As the storm subsided,

They said goodbye to the guest,

And set out.

Many days passed.

Thorri often lifted

The hammer when necessary.

Many different creatures,

Some of them nameless,

He struck down with a blow,

Powerful and brave.

Lok scouted out the land.

With his cunning tricks,

He sneaked into the dwellings

of snow giants.

After stealing food,

He returned to his brothers.

Wald, full of advice,

Knew the habits of monsters

And taught his brothers

How to avoid them.

Thus they reached the sea.

The end of their journey was close.

Massive mountains nearby

Were the borders of this world.

There, in the distance,

Burned a flame brighter than the sun.

It was their destination,

The end of distant wanderings.

t:
The brothers found there

 A wonderful old man

With a white beard,

Wearing scarlet clothes.

"Are you called Num?"

Lok asked fearlessly.

"Teach us, old one,

How to avoid Fate!"

"Foolish children!"

Num answered angrily.

"In vain

you came to my halls!

I do know of a way

To avoid fate.

But it is infeasible

For the Sparks of mortals!

To argue with fate,

You must be free

Of all the chains

And fetters of the world.

But you are held tightly

By the Thread of Fate,

A vigilant Weaver

Spun it before your birth."

The brothers listened,

And in heavy thoughts

Set out for home.

Their families were waiting.

Within reach...

Bells are ringing!

This means the Orcs

Attacked viciously again.

The brothers did not wait -

Rushed to help!

A hard-won victory -

The brothers survived

Miraculously in this battle.

Such is the will of Fate!

Accepting the Threads,

The Gibberling brothers

Resigned themselves

To their great fate.

Future alliances

Needed a base

They were destined to build.

Votin gave Thorri

His mighty troops,

Lok will appease the Zvergs.

Wald will think of a way

To approach the harsh Pridens.

Great-grandchildren will continue

Their Threads in the Pattern.

What is meant to be will happen!

The Orcs will be gone from Isa!

Sagas will remember

Thorri, Lok, and Wald!

The glory of the Gibberlings

Is preserved for centuries!

t:

Before Yok destroyed the sea, it was customary to scatter the ashes over water, and especially revered representatives of the people were sent on their last voyage in a small boat which was set on fire by a shot from a distance.

Now no one wants to send the ashes of their dead to the unknown and frightening abyss of Ginnungagap!

This is how the Stone Boats appeared - the outlines of the ships that you see here laid out on the ground with rocks. Inside the boat, the ashes of members of the same clan are buried, and their names are written on the stones that form the sides. This is how the old forgotten tradition of the "family ship" is preserved, and the deceased get the opportunity to go with their family on a happy "endless journey".

t:
Everything in our settlement is run by the Elder, the most respected Gibberling of their clan. There is a council where the heads of all the clans and other respected Gibberlings decide on issues that affect all of our people.

A Chief Elder can be chosen among the Elders - they are responsible for military affairs and other events, so usually it's the Elder of the Stalwart clan. Once upon a time, it was the Chief Elders who made agreements with the Heidruns, Pridens and Zvergs, but now we only do business with the Heidruns whose leader usually lives in the Meadmakers' village. We do not have dealings with the Urun - we only fight them.

The decision of the Elders is the law, and they are rarely challenged. All in all, the community is a big team that shares sorrows and joys. A clan is a large family where several different generations exist together, connected by intricate family threads...

We value family above all else, and the worst crime is a crime against our clan and especially our sprout. The capital punishment is exile and renunciation.

The exile, or "skogarmaor", is deprived of all rights, separated from the sprout, and forced to survive alone in the frosty lands! Their thread in the tribe's Carpet of Fate is cut off, and the criminal is "dead" for the community. The sprout has the option to go into exile with them.

We do not believe in immortality and therefore place high value on life. If fate favors the traitor, they will be able to survive even in harsh conditions, and then the council of clans, perhaps, will consider the option of pardoning them.

A less severe punishment is the Judgment of Fate, a difficult test that the offender must pass. For example, defeat a powerful monster that lives in the lands of deadly frost and come back alive. Few people manage that, but if Fate favors them, they will be exonerated!

The idea of interwoven Threads is also reflected in the community's Carpet of Fate. On the birthday of a sprout, the community's Thread Keepers measure out threads for them, which are then woven into one and then used in the overall Pattern. They try to measure out a great length of thread to ensure a long life for the sprout.

And the tradition of braiding hair into many braids is still widespread among the Gibberlings of both sexes. It is also believed that Emla's ability to influence the weaving of the Threads of her descendants makes her the first Weaver in history!
r522479.n: Tell me more about the Threads

t: From that came the unique feature of our people. Each Gibberling in a sprout has their own Thread, and the Threads of the sprout are tightly intertwined. Therefore, the families of our people always try to stick together and protect each other.
